source_observation: At the pinned F2 source, verify_release_archive receives the entire archive as bytes, materializes every member via member_bytes = {info.filename: archive.read(info.filename) for info in infos}, and then materializes canonical_archive_bytes by rebuilding the full deterministic ZIP before comparing it to archive_bytes.

local_reproducer.environment: Linux 6.18.35 x86_64; Python 3.13.5; isolated ChatGPT container; not F2 target VPS or user host
local_reproducer.method: Create canonical-style ZIP_STORED archives containing one payload plus a small manifest. Start tracemalloc only after archive_bytes already exists, then execute the source-observed memory mechanism: ZipFile(BytesIO(archive_bytes)) -> read all members into a dictionary -> rebuild a second ZIP_STORED archive in memory. Record Python-tracked peak allocation.

observed_result: Across 1-64 MiB payloads, the reproduced source mechanism showed stable approximately-linear Python-tracked peak incremental allocation at about 2.125x archive size. The input archive bytes were allocated before tracemalloc started, so this ratio is incremental verifier allocation and not total process RSS.
interpretation: The source-predicted memory amplification mechanism is real in a controlled reproduction. For current ZIP_STORED v1, generic decompression-ratio defenses are lower-value than replacing all-at-once member retention plus full in-memory canonical re-encoding in the install lane with manifest-bound streaming verification against a trusted exact ReleaseArchiveReceipt.
limitations: This was not execution of the complete F2 module because the connected GitHub source could not be materialized into the isolated runtime through the available connector/file bridge in this run.
The reproducer mirrors the exact relevant allocation pattern but omits unrelated F2 validation branches and therefore is mechanism evidence, not full exact-source F2 runtime evidence.
tracemalloc measures Python-tracked allocations and is not a complete process-RSS profiler.
No target VPS, clean local host, installer flow, effect path or whole-system runtime was executed.

counterhypothesis_status.hypothesis: The all-at-once verifier memory cost may be negligible for actual F2 release sizes.
counterhypothesis_status.reason: Scaling is reproduced, but no canonical production-sized release artifact was benchmarked in this run. Urgency depends on actual release size and host memory envelope.

next_exact_gate: Trigger4 should benchmark the exact F2 verifier at a representative release size and implement/test a path-or-seekable-file streaming install-lane verifier only if the measured memory budget is material. The candidate should require exact expected ReleaseArchiveReceipt identity, stream artifact/member hashes and byte counts, reuse ReleaseManifest exact sizes, and avoid a second full archive materialization. Keep build-time canonical encoding verification separate.
